decisions.decision: THE DECISIVE MEASUREMENT: the caller already exists and is already carried. internal/api/api.go:114 calls application.LoopCaller(h.config.ReconcileIdentity) and internal/api/api.go:119 passes application.ContextWithCaller(r.Context(), loop) into h.config.InternalReconcile; cmd/control-plane/main.go:199-207 is that closure, and it already runs inside a 5s context (main.go:200). Measured at 81eef87: Service.Plan gates on callerActor(ctx, RoleOwner, RoleScheduler) at internal/application/service.go:888 and Service.Prepare on the same pair at :1023. So the reachability repair needs NO new caller producer, NO new authority, NO new transport and NO new port on the Loop side: it needs one method on Service gated callerActor(ctx, RoleScheduler) and one call added to a closure that already exists and already carries the identity. Everything else in this task is the observation each transition must carry.
decisions.rationale: Framing this as 'three paths need callers' would have produced three identities, and the shortest way to get three identities is to let each path name itself -- which is precisely non_goal 1 and precisely what internal/runner/orchestrator.go:54 already does with RoleRunner. Framing it as 'the identity is already in the tick; what is missing is a pass that uses it' fixes the location (one file in internal/application), fixes the authority (scheduler only), and moves the entire risk surface onto the observations and the bound, which is where it belongs. V2-086 built the mechanism and V2-086's own scan (internal/application/requested_by_test.go:369-372, re-measured: 93 non-test files, exactly 1 RoleScheduler Caller literal) is what keeps it single.

decisions.decision: THE THREE APPEARANCES ARE ONE DEFECT AND ONE REPAIR. Measured with `grep -rn '\b<name>\b' --include='*.go' . | grep -v _test.go | grep -v internal/domain/model.go` at 81eef87: RequirementWait 0 hits, RequirementRecover 0, RequirementEvaluate 0, RequirementStart 0, RequirementPause 0, RequirementCancel 0, CompleteRequirementFromRelease 1 (a comment at internal/application/framing.go:30). Separately, internal/application/service.go:993 is the only line in the repository that constructs a domain.Increment outside a test, its only non-test caller is internal/runner/orchestrator.go:59, and Orchestrator is constructed at exactly two sites, internal/runner/orchestrator_test.go:65 and :139 -- both tests. release.Pipeline.Promote (internal/release/pipeline.go:38) has zero non-test callers. Four unreachable transition families, one cause: no component that holds an identity was asking. The repair is ONE bounded pass, Service.LoopPass, in ONE new file internal/application/loop.go, with four stages, one identity and one report.
decisions.rationale: The nine-task split was a convention artefact (v2-task-dag.md 12.1) and re-splitting it inside the design would reproduce it. Naming the single mechanism up front is what makes the three outcomes verifiable as one thing: one caller gate to assert, one bound to measure, one report to read. It also makes the non-goals checkable, because every non-goal is a property of the same pass rather than of three different mechanisms.

decisions.decision: CALLER IDENTITY, PATH BY PATH, WITH NO SECOND PRODUCER. (i) The reconcile pass (waiting, recovering), (ii) the Increment-creation stage and (iii) the promotion stage all run inside Service.LoopPass, which gates on callerActor(ctx, RoleScheduler) and on that role ALONE -- not RoleOwner, not RoleRunner. The only producer of that role stays application.LoopCaller (internal/application/caller.go:66); the pass constructs no Caller of its own and internal/application/caller.go is PROHIBITED so it cannot. (iv) The journey driver's identity is a runner session established by runner.Service.VerifySession at the transport (internal/api/auth.go), never named by the driver: the driver holds an opaque session token and the server decides who it is. internal/runner/orchestrator.go:54 fabricates application.Caller{Role: application.RoleRunner, Subject: o.RunnerID, RunnerID: o.RunnerID} with no session verification whatsoever, so wiring Orchestrator into a shipped binary would ship exactly non_goal 1. That single measured line is why the real driver goes over the transport and why the Orchestrator stays test-only.
decisions.rationale: V2-086 relabelled the Orchestrator's OWNER half from a fabricated literal to an injected field, and stopped there; the RUNNER half at :54 is still self-naming and is invisible to every authority test in the suite because the only caller is a test that supplies its own identity anyway. An implementer told to 'give the journey a non-test caller' will reach for the Orchestrator first, because it is the only journey driver that exists -- and the cheapest way to run it in production is to keep :54. Recording the measurement here and prohibiting internal/runner/orchestrator.go turns that from a judgement call into a build constraint.

decisions.decision: THE WAITING SET IS DERIVED FROM THE SCHEDULER'S OWN CLOSED SET, NOT CHOSEN, AND IT IS TWO OF SEVEN. scheduler.AllReasons (internal/scheduler/decision.go:52-60) is a closed, exhaustively-tested set of seven. Measured against what internal/application.BuildAllocationSnapshot (allocation.go:447-484) can actually produce: unmet-dependency is UNREACHABLE (the rows built at allocation.go:460-467 carry no Dependencies field at all), repository-unavailable is UNREACHABLE (Snapshot.Repositories is one synthetic entry with no FailureCount and no IsolatedUntil, allocation.go:478), not-executable is UNREACHABLE (Assessment is never set, so scheduler/decision.go:153's branch cannot fire). Reachable: not-ready, already-owned, resource-conflict (two ready Requirements linked to the same Repository share the contention key 'repository:'+id, allocation.go:362-367) and no-runner-capacity (scheduler/scheduler.go:163-164, when chooseRunner finds no spare capacity). The waiting subset is therefore exactly {resource-conflict, no-runner-capacity} -- the product's 'capacity' condition. EXCLUDED WITH REASONS: already-owned means the Requirement holds an active Lease, i.e. work in flight, not a wait; not-ready is not a condition being awaited at all and its Requirements are in statuses domain.DecideRequirement refuses RequirementWait from anyway (model.go:490-493 admits ready, active, recovering only). The pass must switch exhaustively over all seven so that a future snapshot change surfaces here rather than silently widening the set.
decisions.rationale: Choosing the set by taste is how non_goal 2 gets violated, and the intuitive answer is measurably wrong in BOTH directions. Taking all six non-empty reasons would move a captured or framing Requirement toward waiting on a 'not-ready' verdict that says nothing about a condition; taking only no-runner-capacity would miss resource-conflict, which is the genuine contention case the contention key at allocation.go:362 was built to report and which docs/architecture/domain-model.md:267 names ('dependency, capacity, time'). Deriving from scheduler.AllReasons intersected with what the existing snapshot builder can emit gives one answer, gives it a closed-set guard, and makes the three unreachable reasons a recorded measurement instead of an invisible assumption.

decisions.decision: WAITING IS ISSUED FROM `ready` ONLY, AND THAT IS A MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN A CHOICE. AllocationSchedulerStatus (internal/application/allocation.go:382-392) maps domain ready to scheduler.StatusReady, active to StatusAssigned, completed to StatusCompleted and EVERY other domain status to the empty status; scheduler.structurallyReady (internal/scheduler/scheduler.go:192-202) returns false unless Status == StatusReady. Therefore the scheduler can only ever attach resource-conflict or no-runner-capacity to a Requirement whose domain status is `ready`; an `active` or `recovering` Requirement is always reported not-ready. So this task issues RequirementWait from ready and from nothing else, and the two other source statuses domain.DecideRequirement admits (active, recovering, model.go:491) stay UNISSUED, recorded as a measurement and asserted nowhere.
decisions.rationale: An implementer who wants 'active -> waiting' to work will be tempted to widen AllocationSchedulerStatus or to invent a second snapshot mapping. Both are wrong: allocation.go:382-392's comment states that inventing a scheduler status for a domain status the scheduler declares none for would be adding a decision rule, and a second mapping is the second vocabulary the same file (allocation.go:255-275) already refuses on the reason side. Stopping at ready with the measurement recorded is the honest boundary, and it is exactly the shape V2-084 used when it stopped at five refused edges.

decisions.decision: RECOVERING'S OBSERVATION IS THE ARTEFACT THE SHIPPED RECONCILER ALREADY WRITES, READ THROUGH TWO PORTS THAT ALREADY EXIST. internal/reconciler/reconciler.go:41 Tick expires an Active Lease past its TTL; recoverOne calls domain.MarkExecutionLost and, when the Increment exists, issues domain.IncrementRecover, returning the Increment to ready. docs/product/user-facing-spec.md:275 defines recovering as 'failureまたはRunner消失後、安全な再開を行っている' and docs/architecture/domain-model.md:270 as 'lost ExecutionやPreview failureから再開中'. So the observation is: the Requirement has an Increment for which an Execution exists in domain.ExecutionLost. The pass reads it with application.RequirementReadRepository.IncrementsForRequirements (internal/application/ports.go:123) and ExecutionsForIncrements (:124) -- both already declared, both already implemented by both stores, both batched over exactly the ids on the page the pass already read. Zero new ports, zero store edits, zero domain edits.
decisions.rationale: The obvious place to put a Requirement-level recover is inside internal/reconciler/reconciler.go's recoverOne, one line under the existing IncrementRecover -- and it is wrong for a measured reason: recoverOne's actor is domain.NewActorID('reconciler') (reconciler.go:122), a string the component makes up for itself, and internal/reconciler holds no application.Caller at all. Adding the Requirement transition there would give it an identity it is not, in a package that structurally cannot hold the right one. Putting it in the application layer keeps the actor derived from callerActor, keeps internal/reconciler byte-unchanged, and makes the reconciler's output an OBSERVATION the pass reads rather than a side effect the pass hides inside.

decisions.decision: THE COMPLETION PROOF, ITS SOLE CONSTRUCTOR, AND THE STRUCTURAL GUARD. domain.StableReleaseProof (internal/domain/release.go:117) is a struct whose only field is an unexported pointer to an unexported type, and whose validity predicate valid() (:119-121) is unexported, so no code outside internal/domain can build a valid one by any means other than calling a function that returns one. The sole such function is domain.CompletePromotionWithProof (internal/domain/release.go:150-157). Its only non-test caller is release.PromotionGate (internal/release/release.go:261), whose only non-test caller is release.Pipeline.Promote (internal/release/pipeline.go:52), which has ZERO non-test callers today. domain.CompleteRequirementFromRelease (internal/domain/model.go:529) refuses anything but RequirementEvaluating and refuses an invalid proof with ErrEvidenceIncomplete. THE GUARD IS THREE-LAYERED: (1) internal/domain/** is PROHIBITED, so the shortest wrong answer -- export a proof constructor, or make the field settable -- requires opening a file the task may not touch; (2) internal/release/release.go and internal/release/pipeline.go are PROHIBITED, so no second gate can be introduced beside the one that earns the proof; (3) a new go/ast source guard, internal/application/completion_proof_guard_test.go, asserts over every non-test .go file in the repository that the number of call sites of domain.CompleteRequirementFromRelease is exactly ONE and that it is in internal/application/loop.go, and that the number of call sites of release.Pipeline.Promote and release.PromotionGate outside internal/release is exactly ONE and also in internal/application/loop.go. NON-VACUITY IS PROVEN BY EXECUTION, not asserted: the implementer deletes the real call site, runs the guard, records the RED verdict line and the exact failure message, restores the call site, and records the GREEN verdict line -- the technique V2-087 used.
decisions.rationale: A convention ('only the promotion path builds the proof') is unenforceable and this repository already knows it: internal/scheduler/source_guard_test.go, internal/store/memory/source_guard_test.go, internal/runner/source_guard_test.go and internal/release/source_guard_test.go all exist because a prose claim about source structure cannot fail a build. Prohibiting internal/domain is V2-089's technique and it is worth more here than anywhere, because the proof's unexported-pointer design is ALREADY the structure -- the only way to defeat it is to edit the package that declares it. And a guard that has never been observed red is a guard whose message nobody has read: the delete-and-observe step is what turns 'exactly one call site' from a number into a tripwire.

decisions.decision: THE NEGATIVE TEST THAT SEPARATES 'THE INCREMENT SUCCEEDED' FROM 'THE REQUIREMENT MAY COMPLETE'. Product authority, quoted and cited: docs/architecture/domain-model.md:101 '1 Requirementに複数Incrementを許す。Incrementが成功してもRequirementは自動完了しない。'; docs/product/definition.md:105 'システム上の改善完了は、対象変更がPreviewで実証され、Stableへ昇格した時点とする。'; definition.md:130 '完了を自己申告だけで決めず、要求と不変条件を検証する'. THE TEST: drive a Requirement to active, plan an Increment, claim it, start and accept a SUCCEEDING Execution, carry the Increment to released, and run the pass with a release candidate whose promotion criteria are UNMET -- a declared capability with no evidence, which internal/domain/release.go:98-102 refuses by name with ErrEvidenceIncomplete. Assert: release.Pipeline.Promote returns an error, the pass reports zero evaluations and zero completions, and the Requirement is byte-identical by reflect.DeepEqual INCLUDING Version and INCLUDING StableSnapshot. A SECOND negative in the same table: promotion SUCCEEDS and returns a valid proof, but the Requirement's Increments are not all released -- assert no evaluate and no completion for that Requirement while a sibling Requirement whose Increments ARE all released does complete in the same pass.
decisions.rationale: The first negative is the one the outcome names; the second is the one that catches the opposite error, where a successful promotion is treated as a licence to complete everything in flight. Together they pin the completion to the conjunction of two independent observations -- a proof the promotion path earned, and this Requirement's own Increments having reached released -- so neither half alone can move a Requirement. Asserting byte-equality including Version is what makes 'nothing happened' checkable rather than inferred from a status that happened not to change.

decisions.decision: THE BOUND: reuse the existing bounded read exactly, and repair the one place it throws away the truth. The pass's read cost per invocation is a fixed set of bounded reads, none of which grows with the Requirement count: one u.RequirementsPage(ctx, cursor, scheduler.MaxCandidates) page (MaxCandidates = 100, internal/scheduler/scheduler.go:15), one u.RequirementRepositoryLinks batch over exactly those ids, one u.ActiveLeases(ctx, AllocationLeaseBound+1) read that FAILS CLOSED above 100 with ErrAllocationLeaseBound (internal/application/allocation.go:88,93), one u.IncrementsForRequirements batch and one u.ExecutionsForIncrements batch over the same page. BuildAllocationSnapshot itself fails closed above scheduler.MaxCandidates with ErrAllocationCandidateBound rather than truncating (allocation.go:455-458). THE MEASURED DEFECT TO REPAIR WHILE REUSING IT: allocation.go:603 reads `candidates, _, err := u.RequirementsPage(ctx, "", scheduler.MaxCandidates)` -- the `more` flag is DISCARDED, so the existing owner read cannot say whether it saw everything. The pass must capture it, must carry an opaque cursor across invocations, and its report must state MoreRequirementsExist, the cursor, the page size and a per-pass cap on transitions. What one pass leaves unexamined is exactly the Requirements after the cursor, and the way a later pass reaches them is the next tick with the carried cursor -- which must be asserted by a test that seeds more Requirements than one page, runs two passes, and proves the second pass transitions a Requirement the first did not see.
decisions.rationale: Correctness wants every Requirement examined and the quota machinery bounds every read, and the failure mode is not the bound: it is silent truncation that reads as 'covered everything'. This repository already has the right idiom in two flavours -- fail closed above the bound (BuildAllocationSnapshot) and report the remainder (ReleaseRetentionView.MoreRequirementsExist, internal/application/release_surface.go:270). Reusing them costs nothing and makes the omission auditable. Measured cost is now meaningful on both adapters because V2-087 landed: internal/store/memory/store.go:353 calls quota.Counter.TrueUp with the same correction internal/store/firestore/store.go:495 applies, so a read/write count measured in memory is the count the real adapter reserves.

decisions.decision: THE REAL DRIVER AND WHAT RunFakeJourney KEEPS. Orchestrator.RunFakeJourney (internal/runner/orchestrator.go:46) STAYS, byte-unchanged, test-only: measured 3 call sites, all in internal/runner/orchestrator_test.go (:68, :75, :140), and 2 Orchestrator composite literals, both in that file (:65, :139). internal/runner/orchestrator.go is PROHIBITED. The real driver differs in five measurable ways. (1) It does NOT Capture: RunFakeJourney calls Service.Capture at orchestrator.go:55 and so manufactures the very Requirement it then works on -- a journey that invents its own input is the fake this task refuses. The real driver only claims work the Loop pass planned for a Requirement an owner captured. (2) It does NOT fabricate a runner Caller (orchestrator.go:54); its identity is a session the server verified. (3) It does NOT call Provider.Run: all three adapters return NoExec (internal/provider/adapters.go), and no Provider CLI invocation is authorised for this task, so the driver stops at the provider boundary and posts NO result it did not obtain. (4) It is BOUNDED: at most MaxDriverClaims Increments per run, and a single pass over the offered page. (5) It runs in a process it did not construct, talking HTTP to a control plane it does not share memory with.
decisions.rationale: 'Wire up the journey driver we already have' is the cheapest answer and it is wrong on four of these five counts at once, which is why each one is written down as a difference rather than as a scope note. Keeping RunFakeJourney means the existing journey assertions keep passing unedited, so the new driver has to earn its own proof instead of inheriting one; and keeping it prohibited means an implementer cannot make the new driver pass by relaxing the old one.

decisions.decision: THE ONE ROUTE THIS TASK ADDS, AND WHY IT IS UNAVOIDABLE. POST /v1/runner/claims:acquire requires a caller-supplied increment_id and expected_increment_version (internal/api/api.go:1079-1090 and claimBody), and there is NO runner-readable route that lists claimable Increments: the runner-role POST routes are exactly the four at internal/api/api.go:384-397 and there is no runner GET at all. GET /v1/queue/summary and GET /v1/export are owner-only (internal/application/allocation.go:559, readmodels.go). So a separate-process Runner cannot discover work by any means, and no amount of client code fixes that. This task therefore adds exactly one bounded runner-role read, GET /v1/runner/work, backed by Service.OfferedWork in the same new file, derived from the SAME bounded page the pass uses and returning at most a named cap of {increment_id, expected_increment_version, requirement_id} triples for Increments in domain.IncrementReady, with no text, no packet, no digest and no credential-shaped field.
decisions.rationale: An implementer who does not measure this will write the client first and discover at integration that the driver has nothing to ask for -- and the tempting repair at that point is to have the test tell the driver which Increment to claim, which is the fake journey wearing a different hat. Adding the read as a first-class, contract-declared route keeps the discovery on the server where the authority is, keeps it bounded by the same constant, and keeps the driver honest: it claims what it was offered and nothing else.

decisions.decision: cmd/runner STOPS BEING A STUB WITH ZERO ci/components.json MOVEMENT, AND THE ALTERNATIVES ARE STRUCTURALLY FORBIDDEN. Measured in ci/components.json: the `runner` component's roots are ['cmd/runner/**','cmd/bootstrap/**','internal/runner/**'], so cmd/runner importing internal/runner is INTRA-component and declares no edge; the new client imports only net/http, encoding/json and standard library. Measured: internal/runner contains ZERO files importing net/http (`grep -ln 'net/http' internal/runner/*.go` returns nothing), so the client is genuinely new rather than a refactor. The two alternatives are forbidden by structure, not by preference: cmd/runner importing internal/store/firestore would declare runner -> store-firestore while store-firestore already declares runner as a dependency (ci/components.json), i.e. a cycle in the dependency graph that verification_dependencies exists precisely to avoid; and cmd/runner importing internal/store/memory would put a test-only adapter in a shipped binary, which is the fake this task refuses and which DECLARATION-GAP.md already records as absent from the shipped import closure. Consequently ci/components.json and Makefile are PROHIBITED, and a red manifest check means the design was departed from.
decisions.rationale: Rule 9 permits a components.json edit when an edge genuinely moves, and touching ci/** moves all 23 evidence keys because ci/** is in all_on_change. Measuring first showed that no edge moves at all, which converts a large, key-moving, cycle-risking change into no change -- and converts the prohibition into a tripwire: if the manifest goes red, the implementer imported something the design did not sanction.

decisions.decision: THE RELEASE OBSERVER WIRING CLOSES A SECOND LEDGER ROW IN THE SAME COMMIT, WITHOUT A NEW IMPORT EDGE. Measured: Service.AttachReleaseObserver (internal/application/release_surface.go:51) and NewSourceReleaseObserver (:121) have ZERO non-test callers -- every hit is in internal/application/release_surface_test.go or provider_compatibility_test.go -- and cmd/control-plane/main.go attaches nothing, so GET /v1/release/state returns 503 through internal/api/api.go:900 on the shipped binary. The promotion stage needs the same three things the observer needs: an assembled source root, a release Router and a release Store. internal/application ALREADY imports internal/release (release_surface.go:35); cmd/control-plane does NOT and its declared dependencies are api, application, reconciler, runner and store-firestore. So the wiring is an application-level constructor that takes a ROOT STRING plus a repository and an environment class and builds release.NewRouter and release.NewMemoryStore internally, and cmd/control-plane never imports internal/release. Absent configuration is preserved exactly: no root configured means no observer attached, GET /v1/release/state stays 503, and the promotion stage is SKIPPED and says so in the report.
decisions.rationale: This is the difference between a wiring gap and a defaulted lie. release_surface.go:17-23 already records why no default root exists -- a defaulted root would make the process report a version it was not assembled from -- so the configuration must be explicit and its absence must be a skip rather than a fallback. Doing this in the application layer rather than in cmd is not a style choice: it is the only placement that adds no declared component edge, and it makes the owner's read and the promotion path agree by construction because they share one Router.

decisions.decision: THE GRADE THIS CLAIM STOPS AT, STATED ONCE AND ENFORCED AS A FORBIDDEN SENTENCE. docs/architecture/release-contract.md:52 defines preview-local as the owner's own machine running the candidate version's Control Plane AND Runner as real processes on localhost with a Firestore emulator as canonical store, and release-contract.md:56 lists the four things preview-local cannot establish -- IAP authentication boundary, scale-to-zero, real Firestore permissions and contention, and the deploy path -- all of which belong to D1. v2-task-dag.md G3.2 makes preview-local the real-environment grade for a condition about the Loop's own observable behaviour and explicitly refuses to call it a substitute; G3.3 says unit, fake, stub and contract evidence satisfies no real-environment condition at any grade; 8.1 says a safety condition is satisfied by refusal and a reachability condition by occurrence. THEREFORE: the reachability claims for waiting, for recovering, for Increment creation and for a separate-process Runner claiming and starting an Execution stop at preview-local. The claim for the COMPLETION transition stops at COMPONENT (in-process) grade, because the shipped configuration cannot assemble a fully-evidenced candidate and this task fabricates none. FORBIDDEN VERBATIM, in the records and in any summary: 'this was observed on Cloud Run', 'this was observed in Cloud Logging', 'the deployed environment', 'a Stable promotion occurred', 'all capabilities were exercised', and any capability id.
decisions.rationale: The grade question is where this task is most likely to overclaim, because a real second process and a real emulator FEEL like production. 8.2 already records a coordinator getting the grade question wrong by re-observing the wrong exercise, and 8.1's correction 2 records a judge accepting a single occurrence as a safety proof. Writing the stopping point as a forbidden-sentence list rather than as a caveat makes the overclaim a grep-able failure instead of a matter of tone.

decisions.decision: WHAT STAYS UNISSUED, EACH WITH THE MEASUREMENT THAT BLOCKS IT. (i) RequirementPause and RequirementCancel: zero non-test issuers, and they are owner control verbs held by V2-090; issuing pause would also create a one-way door because internal/domain declares no resume command and RequirementReadyCommand is not admitted from paused (model.go:481). (ii) RequirementNeedInput from evaluating: internal/application/human_input.go holds that surface and is PROHIBITED. (iii) The post-execution Increment half -- verify, integrate, preview-validate, accept, release -- has zero non-test issuers anywhere (measured) and needs a verification and integration adapter that does not exist; DECLARATION-GAP.md already holds that row. (iv) RequirementWait from active and from recovering: unreachable from the existing snapshot mapping, see d5. (v) A Requirement whose Increment FAILED rather than went lost: docs/architecture/domain-model.md:275 says such a Requirement becomes recovering, waiting or needs-input, and this task issues recover only on domain.ExecutionLost, so the failed case is recorded and left. None of these is given a task id: they go into row (3) of the scope-boundary table or are noted as already held by DECLARATION-GAP.md.
decisions.rationale: v2-task-dag.md 12.7 puts M5's remediation budget at exactly 5 of 5 and 12.10 says a sixth is a signal that the milestone is mis-cut, so proposing a task id for any of these would be the failure mode the governance change exists to stop. Recording each with the measurement that blocks it is what lets a later reader tell a deliberate stop from an oversight -- and 12.3 gives the implementer the in-task escape hatch if one of them turns out to be load-bearing: revise the boundary, in place, with the pre-revision table and the reason.

decisions.decision: DETERMINISM IS PART OF THE MECHANISM, NOT A TEST STYLE. A reconcile pass and a journey driver are exactly the two things an implementer tests with a sleep, and commit 56ee097 on main had to replace fixed-timeout waits in the lifecycle E2E with wait_for, wait_gone and wait_polls for that reason. Constraints, all measurable: no fixed sleep, no wall-clock timer, no goroutine and no randomness in any new or modified test; every clock injected (the pass reads s.clock.Now() once per invocation and passes that instant down, as allocationReport already requires); the driver takes an injected *http.Client and an injected clock and starts no timer; the client's unit tests use a stub http.RoundTripper and NOT httptest.NewServer -- measured, httptest.NewServer appears ZERO times in this repository today, so introducing it would introduce the goroutine this rule forbids; every wait in the live-local exercise is a bounded deadline poll reusing that file's existing idiom; a measured duration is logged as an observation and never asserted as a threshold; and -race is required on every run.
decisions.rationale: Two of this task's four stages are driven by a tick and the fifth is a second process, so the temptation to synchronise with time rather than with state is structural rather than accidental. Naming the specific substitutes -- injected clock, RoundTripper stub, bounded deadline poll, cursor-carried second pass -- removes the excuse that there was no deterministic way to express the wait.

verification: v1. Re-measure every number in this packet before writing code. The commands are recorded in the Work Order's A2; each was executed by the designer at HEAD 81eef87 and each is expected to be stale. Report BOTH values for every disagreement: V2-085 found twelve and V2-086 found nineteen.

v2. The caller gate. Service.LoopPass returns application.ErrForbidden for an owner Caller and for a runner Caller and application.ErrUnauthenticated for a context with no Caller; a scheduler Caller obtained from application.LoopCaller runs it. Assert all four, and assert that the pass constructs no application.Caller of its own by re-running the V2-086 scan and confirming the repository-wide count of RoleScheduler Caller literals is still exactly ONE.

v3. Waiting. With capacity exhausted (active >= the effective limit), a `ready` Requirement receives exactly one RequirementWait transition, its Version increments by exactly one, and the recorded event carries the scheduler reason string that justified it. With capacity available and no contention, the SAME fixture receives ZERO transitions. With two `ready` Requirements linked to the same Repository, the second receives resource-conflict and transitions; assert the reason recorded is resource-conflict and not no-runner-capacity.

v4. Waiting's closed set. A table test over all seven members of scheduler.AllReasons asserts which two transition and which five do not, and asserts that scheduler.AllReasons has exactly seven members so that a reason added to internal/scheduler fails this test rather than silently joining or leaving the set.

v5. Recovering. A Requirement in `active` with an Increment whose Execution is domain.ExecutionLost receives exactly one RequirementRecover transition and the recorded event names the Execution id and the Increment id that justified it. The same fixture with the Lease still active and the Execution still running receives ZERO transitions. A fixture whose Execution is domain.ExecutionFailed rather than lost receives ZERO transitions, and that is logged as the recorded boundary of d15(v).

v6. The observation is carried, and absence means no transition. For each of waiting, recovering and completion, run the pass with the justifying observation ABSENT and assert zero transitions and the aggregate byte-identical by reflect.DeepEqual including Version. A pass that always advances is the defect; these three are its detector.

v7. Increment creation. In a composed run, a `ready` Requirement the scheduler ASSIGNED gets an Increment planned and prepared by the pass under the scheduler identity, and the Increment is readable afterwards. Assert that a `ready` Requirement the scheduler did NOT assign gets no Increment. Assert the per-pass cap: with more assignable Requirements than the cap, exactly the cap is planned and the report says how many were left.

v8. Promotion and completion.
